record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Polyomino Tilings
record.original_question: Does there exist a set consisting of exactly two polyomino prototiles that tiles the plane but has only non-periodic tilings; that is, an aperiodic set of two polyominoes?

evidence.quote: Here we consider tilings that are not monohedral: the set of prototiles contains multiple polyominoes. The introduction of multiple prototiles enables creating prototile sets that only have non-periodic tilings
Examples of aperiodic sets of just three polyominoes are known ... To the author’s knowledge, no aperiodic set of two polyominoes is known
Open Problem 8 Does there exist an an aperiodic set of two polyominoes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polyomino is a finite, edge-connected union of unit squares from the integer lattice in the plane. A set of polyominoes P = {P_1, ..., P_k} (called prototiles) is said to tile the plane if the plane can be covered, without gaps or overlaps, by congruent copies (under translations, rotations, and reflections) of the elements of P. Such a tiling is periodic if it is invariant under two linearly independent translations, and non-periodic otherwise. The set P is called aperiodic if it admits at least one tiling of the plane and every tiling of the plane by copies of its elements is non-periodic.

Aperiodic sets consisting of exactly three polyominoes are known to exist. Determine whether there exists an aperiodic set consisting of exactly two polyomino prototiles, i.e., a pair {P_1, P_2} of polyominoes that tiles the plane but admits no periodic tiling.
artifact.status_search_result: No aperiodic set of two polyominoes appears to be known. Recent work (2024) establishes results on translational aperiodic sets of 7 polyominoes and undecidability with 8 polyominoes, but the question of whether two polyominoes can form an aperiodic set (allowing rotations/reflections) remains unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Translational Aperiodic Sets of 7 Polyominoes
status_evidence.snippet: Smallest known aperiodic sets for translational tilings have size 7-8; smaller cases remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research focuses on aperiodic polyomino sets of size 7 or more; no aperiodic pair of polyominoes is reported.

status_evidence.title: Undecidability of tiling the plane with a set of 8 polyominoes
status_evidence.snippet: Tiling the plane with a set of 8 polyominoes is undecidable.
status_evidence.claim: Current results address sets of size ≥7; the existence of an aperiodic set of two polyominoes is not established.
